pamphlet_excerpts: Afew Safety Rules: Before you handle a horse, you should know afew safety rules.
Horses Sense Youare: Because horses can sense if youare afraid, be confident yet careful around them.
Prevent Accidents Injuries: Prevent accidents and injuries by followingthese rules. • Ground Safety -Never startle a horse.
Startle Cause Kick: You might startle it and cause it to kick, whichcould result in a serious injury.
step_by_step_procedure: Free-choice Salt Providedby: Free-choice salt can be providedby securing to the stall wall a white salt block that they canaccess as needed.
Horses Left Pasture: Horses left to pasture spend much of their timegrazing on grass.
They Eat Lot: They often have to eat a lot ofgrass to gain enough nutrients.
Pasture Grassis Poor: If the pasture grassis poor in nutrients and vitamins, concentrated feedmix can help provide a more balanced diet.

But Learn Theparts: But first, learn theparts of a horse so that you can discuss them with confidence.
Variety Natural Markings: A variety of natural markings and coat colors gives horses theirdistinct looks.
Horse Breeds Varied: Because horse breeds can be as varied as breeds of otheranimals, such as dogs and cats, it is important to weigh thecharacteristics of each breed.
step_by_step_procedure: Willneed Decide Factors: You willneed to decide what factors are best for the purpose you havein mind for the horse, whether riding for pleasure, workingcattle, showing.
Decide Breed Age: Decide on the breed, age, size, and sex of the horse accordingly.
Owning Horse Expensive: Owning a horse is expensive and time-consuming, sofirst determine why you want one.
Deciding Areable Handle: Deciding whether you areable to handle the responsibility and expense takes greatconsideration.

pamphlet_excerpts: Horses Built Forage: Although horses are built to forage, it is not always practicalto put a horse out to pasture.
There Few Rules: When feeding, there are a few rules to follow. • Provide an amount of feed appropriate to the horse’s activity level.
Too Feed Cause: Too much feed can cause digestive and circulatoryproblems.
Too Little Feed: Too little feed can lead to a loss of energy, and itcould harm the horse’s overall condition.
step_by_step_procedure: Horseis Stabled Giveit: If your horseis stabled, giveit clean waterbefore feeding. • Do not feed a horse that is tired or overheated.
Horsecool Off Sufficiently: Let a horsecool off sufficiently after exercise or work before allowingit to eat. • Water is critical for a horse’s health.
Produce Salivaand Fluids: It helps produce salivaand other fluids, regulates body temperature, carries nutrientsthrough the body, and is important for digestion.
Horsecan Drink Gallons: A horsecan drink from 4 to 15 or more gallons of water each day, depending on the weather, amount of work, and its ageand size.

Horse Sconformation Critical: A horse’sconformation is a critical indication of its soundness and ability.
Well-proportioned Horse: A well-proportioned horse will be well-balanced, which allowsit to move efficiently and makes it less prone to unsoundnessand strain.
Well-balanced Conformation: A well-balanced conformation will give the horse alonger working life and help it maintain a better temperament.
step_by_step_procedure: Choose Yourhorse: As you choose yourhorse, keep the followingthings in mind.
Shouldbe Muscular Themuscles: It shouldbe muscular and themuscles should look evenlybuilt, giving the horse abalanced shape.
Well-shapedhead Proportionalto: Look for a well-shapedhead that is proportionalto the rest of the body.
Ahead Too Big: Ahead that is too big or smallwill upset the balance of thehorse’s overall appearance.

pamphlet_excerpts: Horse Usefulness Depends: A horse’s usefulness depends greatly on thecondition of its hooves, which need dailyinspection and attention to stay healthy.
Long-term Exposure: In addition, long-term exposure to bacteriacan lead to infections.
Starting Horse Weeks: Starting when a horse is about 6 weeks old, the hoovesshould be leveled with a rasp (file) by a horseshoer (farrier) to prevent the bones from growing.
Lifting Inspecting: Lifting, inspecting, and cleaningthe hooves daily will prepare the horse for thepossible next step of shoeing.
step_by_step_procedure: Hoof Pick Carefully: Use the hoof pick to carefully clean thebottom of each hoof from heel to toe.
Rasping Shoeing Doneonly: Rasping and shoeing should be doneonly by a farrier.
Hoof Pick Probably: A hoof pick probably will be the most importantitem in your grooming kit.
Shoes Preventexcessive Hoof: Shoes help preventexcessive hoof wear under rocky conditions.

Halter Horse Tie: Step 1, Put a halter on the horse and tie it to a secure fence, rail, or post attachment with a quick-release knot.
Surethe Horse Standing: Make surethe horse is standing square with its weight evenly distributed.
Stand Beside Horse: Step 2, Stand beside the horse’s left foreleg, facing towardthe tail.
step_by_step_procedure: Run Left Hand: Run your left hand down the leg so the horse is awarethat you are going to do something.

pamphlet_excerpts: Horses Built Forage: Although horses are built to forage, it is not always practicalto put a horse out to pasture.
There Few Rules: When feeding, there are a few rules to follow. • Provide an amount of feed appropriate to the horse’s activity level.
Too Feed Cause: Too much feed can cause digestive and circulatoryproblems.
Too Little Feed: Too little feed can lead to a loss of energy, and itcould harm the horse’s overall condition.
step_by_step_procedure: Horseis Stabled Giveit: If your horseis stabled, giveit clean waterbefore feeding. • Do not feed a horse that is tired or overheated.
Horsecool Off Sufficiently: Let a horsecool off sufficiently after exercise or work before allowingit to eat. • Water is critical for a horse’s health.
Produce Salivaand Fluids: It helps produce salivaand other fluids, regulates body temperature, carries nutrientsthrough the body, and is important for digestion.
Horsecan Drink Gallons: A horsecan drink from 4 to 15 or more gallons of water each day, depending on the weather, amount of work, and its ageand size.

Teach Horse Move: As you teach your horse to move backward with a halter, remember that horses dislike moving backward.
Horse Sfirst Reaction: Your horse’sfirst reaction might be to raise its head and plant its hind feet.
However There Effective: However, there is an effective way to teach your horse to back up.
step_by_step_procedure: Stand Left Side: Step 1, Stand on the left side of the horse, near thewithers, with the lead rope in your right hand.
Rope Tobump Horse: Use the rope tobump the horse’s forefeet back while using your left hand tokeep the horse’s nose straight.
Move Horse Back: Just move the horse back a step at a time while saying “back.” It might help to have the horse facing a wall sothat it can’t go forward.
Horse Won Move: Step 2, If the horse won’t move, push the horse at thechest, where the muscles join.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include—with your parent or guardian's permission—an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby or healthy lifestyle. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.
